text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Industrial output growth was reported in 51 percent of Poland's corporate sector, which showed a three percent growth compared with September, while 18 percent of the companies reported a decline over the period, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said .
- Poland's housing industry will not improve significantly by 2010, a recent report by the Housing Economy Institute said.
- The Poznan-based Bahia confectionery maker's turnover this year will reach 16.5 million zlotys and the net profit should not go below 600,000 zlotys, the plant's president Tadeusz Kita said.
- The Czestochowa bank has started issuing Polcard credit cards to customers who have used the bank's (ROR) regular accounts at least for three months.
- The French-Polish Bank Inicjatyw Spoleczno Ekonomicznych (BISE) bank will introduce VISA cards in the first quarter of 1997.
NOWA EUROPA
- Around 70 percent of customers insured previously in the bankrupt Westa, Gryf, or Hestja insurance firms now choose services offered by the PZU or Warta insurance market giants.

- Poland's tobacco market has collapsed after two excise tax rises, by 20 percent each, in the last four months, the Polish tobacco industry association president Jan M. Wierzbicki said. The new tax laws will result in a 10 percent decline in cigaret the production this year.
- A new cutsoms office division has come into operation in Ostrowiec Wielkopolski, western Poland, to service about 40 percent of the locally registered firms.
- All but two plants of the Poznan-based Hipolit Cegielski (HCP) heavy industry complex have already undergone modernisation, the HCP president Waclaw Piotrowski said.
- The listed Zywiec brewery and its trade unions have agreed that jobs need to be cut in the company because one of its plants has recently been closed, the company statement said.

- Poland's Bank Depozytowo Kredytowy (BDK) expects to receive an operating licence from Ukraine's central bank for its fully-owned subsidiary in that country this year, the BDK deputy president Dariusz Blaszczuk said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Wroclaw-based PZL-Hydral aviation firm has received an International Standards Organisation (ISO) 9001 certificate for its quality control system.
- The listed ComputerLand software maker has increased its annual profit forecast from nine to 11 million zlotys.
- Poland's Bank Rozwoju Eksportu (BRE) and the Swiss Pictet et Cie will form a trust fund trading in the unlisted companies' stock and the National Investment Fund (NFI) certificates.
- The Hy Test company has bought a 10 percent stake in the listed Beton Stal construction firm.
- The annual net profit of the Lodz-based Boryszew plastic processor will be nine million zlotys, 25 percent of which will be distributed in dividends, the company board said.
ZYCIE

- The Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy (BH) has taken to court the state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank for the allegedly unlawful takeover of a BH-owned bank account in the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank.
